question: Net new assets by quarter for each of the five, with each firm's own definition of the metric.

claims.text: Quarterly net new assets - Edward Jones: The 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) shows net new assets of $16.4 billion for the quarter ended 2025-06-27, against $19.3 billion a year earlier (-15%). The 10-Q shows $0.4 billion for the second column group in the same table, next to the 874 advisor count.

Quarterly net new assets - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-06-26, published 2026-08-07) shows net new assets of $18 billion for the quarter, against $17 billion in the prior-year quarter (+6%). For the six months it shows $36 billion against $34 billion (+6%).

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley (Wealth Management): The financial supplement (published 2026-01-15) shows net new assets of $122.3 billion for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 and $81.0 billion for the quarter ended 2025-09-30. The comparison column for the quarter ended 2024-12-31 shows $56.5 billion. The supplement shows changes of 51% from the prior quarter and 116% from the year-earlier quarter.

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley (Wealth Management): The 2Q26 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-06-30, published 2026-08-04) says NNA for the current quarter were $148 billion, "of which just over half represented inflows related to IPOs of certain clients in our Workplace channel."

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James (fiscal quarters; the disclosed metric is Domestic Private Client Group net new assets): On the fiscal 2Q25 call (published 2025-04-23, quarter ended 2025-03-31), CEO Paul Shoukry said quarterly domestic net new assets equaled $8.8 billion, a 2.6% annualized growth rate on beginning-of-period domestic PCG assets.

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James: The supplement published 2026-07-22 shows Domestic PCG net new assets of $11,651 million (3.4% annualized) for the quarter ended 2025-06-30. It shows $17,930 million (5.0%) for 2025-09-30 and $30,828 million (8.0%) for 2025-12-31. For 2026-03-31 it shows $22,954 million (5.8%), and for 2026-06-30 $21,692 million (5.5%). The nine-month totals are $34,501 million for 2025 and $75,474 million for 2026.

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James: The earnings release published 2026-01-28 shows Domestic PCG net new assets of $30,828 million (8.0% annualized) for the quarter ended 2025-12-31. The year-earlier quarter was $14,020 million (4.0%).
Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) states that core net new assets for the fourth quarter of 2024 were $114.8 billion, up 51% from the fourth quarter of 2023.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: The 1Q26 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-03-31, published 2026-05-08) shows net new client assets of $139.9 billion against $132.4 billion a year earlier (+6%). It shows core net new client assets of $140.0 billion against $137.7 billion (+2%).

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (published 2026-04-16), CEO Rick Wurster said that, excluding a onetime mutual fund clearing outflow, Schwab attracted $158 billion in core net new assets, a first quarter record. This differs from the $140.0 billion core figure in the 10-Q for the same quarter. The chunks do not reconcile the two.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: In the 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-15), Schwab reports $190.4 billion in core net new assets for the third quarter, an annualized growth rate of 5.8%. The deck shows year-to-date core net new assets of $356 billion for 2025 and $450 billion for 2026. These are year-to-date totals, not single quarters.

Definition - Edward Jones: The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) and the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) define net new assets as cash and securities inflows and outflows, excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) uses the same definition but adds "including fees and commissions". The wording therefore changed between the 10-K and the 2Q26 10-Q.

Definition - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) says NNA represent client asset inflows, including interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows. They exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions. The 1Q26 press release (published 2026-04-15) and the January 2026 strategic update deck give the same definition. The 10-Q says NNA levels are influenced by factors including seasonality, advisor and client attraction and retention, and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows.

Definition - Raymond James: The fiscal 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) defines Domestic PCG net new assets as domestic PCG client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic PCG client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees and other fees. The growth percentage is based on the beginning Domestic PCG AUA balance for the period. This metric covers the domestic Private Client Group, not the whole firm.

Definition - Schwab: Schwab's January 2026 monthly report (published 2026-02-13) says the difference between net new assets and core net new assets is net flows from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs. It defines core net new assets as net new assets before significant one-time inflows or outflows, such as acquisitions/divestitures or extraordinary flows (generally greater than $25 billion) relating to a specific client, and activity from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs. The 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15) says the threshold was $10 billion in prior periods.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's GWIM segment reported $4.6 trillion in client balances at 1Q26 (published 2026-04-15), with Merrill Wealth Management at $3.8 trillion and the Private Bank at $757 billion. The release cites AUM flows of $20 billion for the quarter and $78 billion since 1Q25. No net new assets figure or definition appears in these chunks.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), CFO Alastair Borthwick said GWIM added 6,000 net new affluent households in the quarter. The 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-14) cites about 5K net new $500K+ relationships across Merrill and Private Bank.
adjacent.differs_because: These are counts of net new households or relationships at the GWIM segment level, not net new asset dollars, and they are not Merrill standalone figures.

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America quarterly earnings supplement (GWIM section), noting that GWIM covers Merrill and the Private Bank
